sub_niches: budgeting for Gen Z and Millennials
target_audience: Gen Z and Millennials (18-34), English-speaking, interested in building wealth without get-rich-quick schemes

phase_1_bootstrap.note: High-frequency bootstrap to train the algorithm. Both slots target US EST prime time.

phase_2_steady.note: Reduce cadence once channel has 500+ subscribers and algorithm is seeded.

schedule.longform_cadence: Every 5th topic produced as a 3-5 minute video to accumulate watch hours for YPP

visual_style: Premium hand-drawn mature editorial illustration with blueprint visual language: charcoal navy, paper cream, muted teal and sparse warm gold. Subtle grids and dimensions. Calm readable motion. Alex only in justified host scenes. No neon fintech glow.
narration_notes: Confident but not condescending. Measured pace around 140 wpm. Never hype, never panic. Like a smart friend who happens to know finance.
hook_strategy: Open with a source-backed concrete contrast or provocative question. The stakes must be large enough to justify attention; do not lead with tiny arithmetic examples. Keep assumptions explicit and never imply a guaranteed return. First 2 seconds must create cognitive dissonance.
forbidden_topics: specific stock picks or buy/sell recommendations

ypp_target.watch_hours_or_views: 3M Shorts views OR 4000 longform watch hours

thumbnail_rules: Max 3 bold English words on thumbnail (typeset in post)
Navy / paper cream / muted warm gold — no neon mint
One strong visual metaphor from the Visual Bible
Alex only when the cover is host-led
No red arrows or clickbait borders
Color accent only on key number or word
brand.logo_description: Minimalist rising line with blueprint compass motif. Navy and muted gold on cream or navy field. Hand-drawn editorial, not neon fintech.
example_video_titles: Why Inflation Is Melting Your Savings
The 50/30/20 Rule: Master Your Budget in 60 Seconds
Investing vs. Speculation: The Brutal Difference
Why Your Savings Account Is Lying to You
The Rule of 72: Double Your Money Explained
brand.notes: Active identity: wealth_blueprint_visual_v1 (VISUAL-BIBLE). Neon black-mint is superseded. Never use pure red for loss bait. Avoid sensationalism. Every claim must be sourceable.

research.keyword_strategy: Start with long-tail low-competition queries in weeks 1-4, shift to trending topics after 500 subscribers

april: what to do with tax refund

production.renderer_notes: Remotion is wired (produce_edit REMOTION_REQUIRED). Keep editorial default until two green Remotion Production Order E2Es past script QA; then set renderer to remotion.
narrative_rules: Speak directly to the viewer, firmly and naturally, without breathy acting or hype.
At least one third must give specific achievable actions, not generic encouragement.
Spell out numbers for TTS. Separate adjacent amounts and durations into clear sentences.
Only when the topic requires a multi-year timeline, use ordinal year wording. Never invent a first-year or second-year schedule for a regular savings habit.
Give significant honest stakes, state assumptions and never promise market returns.
Use conditional everyday wording rather than repeated hypothetical hedging.
Distinguish accumulating starting capital from the later investment horizon.
Do not copy reference transcripts. End with one concrete action.
visual_rules: Hand-drawn mature editorial + blueprint language: navy, paper cream, muted teal, sparse warm gold.
Use approved Alex stills only in alex=true layouts; otherwise icon/diagram/comparison compositions.
Choose assets by the scene's meaning. Do not use unrelated clips as filler.
Hold final numbers long enough to read. Continue graphs on consistent axes.
Calm readable motion — no neon flashes, random zoom resets or glitch cuts.
thumbnail_rules: One strong relevant visual and a readable hook
Amounts and time horizons must match the script
Use IF IT GROWS for a conditional rate, never a guarantee
